nodes.name: Image macro
nodes.summary: A picture with bold caption text laid over it, the oldest and broadest family of internet memes.

nodes.name: Object labelling
nodes.summary: A single image whose people or objects are tagged with labels so the scene stands for an unrelated situation.

nodes.name: Reaction image
nodes.summary: A still image, usually a face, posted as a reply to show how the poster feels about something.

nodes.name: Drawn character
nodes.summary: A recurring hand-drawn figure that stands in for a mood or a social type and is endlessly redrawn by others.

nodes.name: Comparison
nodes.summary: A layout that sets two or more panels side by side to contrast options, people or outcomes.

nodes.name: Exploitable
nodes.summary: A source image built so that one part can be swapped or redrawn, inviting endless edits.

nodes.name: Multi-panel comic
nodes.summary: A short strip of sequential panels that tells a joke through a small recurring cast.

nodes.name: Copypasta
nodes.summary: A block of text copied and reposted verbatim or with small edits across forums and comment threads.

nodes.name: Catchphrase
nodes.summary: A short phrase that spreads on its own and is attached to many different images and situations.

nodes.name: Video remix
nodes.summary: A video clip or soundtrack that is re-edited, overdubbed or recombined into new versions.

nodes.name: Wojak
nodes.summary: A simple line drawing of a bald, sad-eyed man used to express longing, regret or quiet melancholy, and the base for a large cast of redrawn variants.

nodes.name: I Know That Feel Bro
nodes.summary: Two Wojaks hugging under the line 'I know that feel bro', posted in reply to a story of shared misfortune.

nodes.name: Crying Wojak
nodes.summary: A red-faced Wojak with tears and clenched teeth, used to depict someone furious or upset at an outcome.
nodes.check_note: Earliest known use is an unsourced comic believed to date from 2014; year is soft.

nodes.name: Wojak Mask
nodes.summary: A crying Wojak holding a smiling mask over his face, used to show someone hiding distress behind a cheerful front.

nodes.name: Pink Wojak
nodes.summary: A pink, screaming Wojak used on trading and crypto boards to depict panic during a market crash.

nodes.name: Brainlet
nodes.summary: A Wojak drawn with a shrunken head or tiny brain, used to mock a take as unintelligent.
nodes.check_note: The term 'brainlet' is first archived on 4chan /sci/ in December 2015; the Wojak image may only date from 2016.

nodes.name: Big Brain Wojak
nodes.summary: A bespectacled Wojak with a hugely enlarged, wrinkled brain, used ironically for overthought or self-satisfied reasoning.

nodes.name: NPC Wojak
nodes.summary: A grey, expressionless Wojak used to cast people as non-player characters who repeat opinions without thinking.

nodes.name: Thirty-Year-Old Boomer
nodes.summary: A sunglasses-wearing Wojak holding an energy drink, mocking a young adult with the tastes and habits of an older generation.

nodes.name: Zoomer
nodes.summary: A youthful Wojak representing a teenage member of Generation Z and their online habits.

nodes.name: Doomer
nodes.summary: A Wojak in a black beanie and hoodie, often smoking, representing a young man resigned to hopelessness about the future.

nodes.name: Doomer Girl
nodes.summary: A female counterpart to the Doomer, drawn in dark clothes with short black hair, sharing his gloomy outlook.

nodes.name: Bloomer
nodes.summary: A content, smiling Wojak created as the hopeful opposite of the Doomer.

nodes.name: Coomer
nodes.summary: A dishevelled, hollow-eyed Wojak used to mock someone ruled by compulsive habits, originally pornography.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia dates its rise to November 2019 (No Nut November); earliest drawings may be earlier.

nodes.name: Consoomer
nodes.summary: A Wojak variant mocking someone whose identity revolves around buying franchise products and merchandise.

nodes.name: Soyjak
nodes.summary: A bearded, bespectacled Wojak with a wide open-mouthed expression, used to caricature naive or performative excitement.

nodes.name: Two Soyjaks Pointing
nodes.summary: Two excited Soyjaks pointing at something placed between them, used to mock overexcitement about a product or reveal.

nodes.name: Yes Chad
nodes.summary: A calm, bearded blond figure who answers a mocking question with a flat 'Yes.', used to show unashamed confidence.
nodes.check_note: Character parent Wojak follows the fixture; Chad is a credible alternative. Format parent Virgin vs. Chad is by analogy (insecure vs confident archetypes): the documented origin (Aug 2019) combines the Grayons meme with a 4chan Nordic/Mediterranean exploitable. Fallback format parent: comparison.

nodes.name: Trad Girl
nodes.summary: A blonde, braided female Wojak in a sundress used to depict an idealised traditionalist woman.

nodes.name: Grug
nodes.summary: A caveman Wojak who speaks in broken, simple sentences, used to argue for blunt common sense over sophistication.
nodes.check_note: Earliest illustration reported October 2017; first widely seen upload February 2019. The fixtures call this node 'grug-early-man'.

nodes.name: Doge
nodes.summary: A photo of the Shiba Inu Kabosu glancing sideways, surrounded by multicoloured Comic Sans phrases in broken English such as 'such wow'.
nodes.check_note: Kabosu photo and the 'doge' spelling both date to 2010, but the Comic Sans 'such wow' format mostly spread in 2012-2013. Root changed from reaction-image to image-macro.

nodes.name: Cheems
nodes.summary: A different Shiba Inu, Balltze, cast as a feeble Doge-like character whose speech adds stray 'm' sounds, as in 'cheemsburbger'.

nodes.name: Swole Doge
nodes.summary: Doge's head on a heavily muscled body, used to stand for strength and an idealised past.

nodes.name: Swole Doge vs. Cheems
nodes.summary: A two-panel image pitting muscular Swole Doge against small, weak Cheems to contrast a strong past with a feeble present.
nodes.check_note: Format parent Virgin vs. Chad is by analogy (strong vs weak contrast) and not documented as a direct derivation; fallback format parent: comparison.

nodes.name: Dogelore
nodes.summary: Deliberately misspelled comics that place Doge and an extended cast of dogs in absurd everyday stories.

nodes.name: Walter
nodes.summary: A close-up of a white bull terrier staring into the camera, captioned as loving fire trucks and 'moster trucks'.
nodes.check_note: Walter is Nelson, a bull terrier, not a Shiba; he spread separately (Sept 2018) and was later absorbed into the Dogelore cast. The character link records cast membership, not descent; alternatives are a parent of Dogelore or a standalone family under reaction-image.

nodes.name: Doge Bonk
nodes.summary: Doge swinging a bat at another dog with the word 'bonk', posted to playfully punish an out-of-line remark.

nodes.name: Pepe the Frog
nodes.summary: A green cartoon frog from Matt Furie's comic Boy's Club that became one of the most reused reaction characters online.

nodes.name: Feels Good Man
nodes.summary: Pepe's contented line from the original comic, reused as a caption or emote for simple satisfaction.

nodes.name: Sad Frog
nodes.summary: A dejected, teary Pepe posted to express disappointment, often captioned 'feels bad man'.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia only says it was in use on Tumblr 'by 2012'; 4chan use is probably earlier (often cited as 2009).

nodes.name: Smug Frog
nodes.summary: A self-satisfied Pepe with a knowing smirk, posted to gloat or feign superiority.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia gives 2012; a 4chan /tv/ post from June 2011 is reported as the earliest instance.

nodes.name: Angry Pepe
nodes.summary: A red-faced, shouting Pepe paired with a long 'REEE' to mock an outburst of frustration.

nodes.name: Rare Pepe
nodes.summary: Original or unusual Pepe drawings presented ironically as rare collectibles to be hoarded and traded.

nodes.name: Apu Apustaja
nodes.summary: A deliberately crude, childlike redraw of Pepe whose name is broken Finnish for 'help helper', spread from the Finnish board Ylilauta.

nodes.name: Peepo
nodes.summary: A small, round, simplified Pepe used as a family of Twitch and Discord emotes.

nodes.name: Pepega
nodes.summary: A Pepe with a huge nose and gaping mouth used on Twitch to call something or someone foolish.

nodes.name: monkaS
nodes.summary: A sweating, anxious Pepe emote used on Twitch during tense or nerve-wracking moments.

nodes.name: PepeHands
nodes.summary: A crying Pepe with hands raised to his face, used on Twitch to express sadness or mock grief.

nodes.name: Sadge
nodes.summary: A simplified, downcast Pepe emote used in Twitch chat for mild disappointment.
nodes.check_note: Reported as created around 2019 and released as an emote in January 2020; year is soft.

nodes.name: Chad
nodes.summary: An idealised, effortlessly confident alpha male archetype, drawn as a tall square-jawed figure.
nodes.check_note: Date is for the drawn Chad figure of Virgin vs. Chad (2017); the slang 'Chad'/'Chad Thundercock' is older (mid-2010s) and may move this date earlier.

nodes.name: Virgin vs. Chad
aliases: The Virgin Walk vs. The Chad Stride
nodes.summary: A side-by-side drawing contrasting a hunched, insecure 'virgin' with a confident 'Chad', applied to any pair of rival things.

nodes.name: Gigachad
nodes.summary: Stylised black-and-white photos of an impossibly chiselled man, used as the ultimate image of confident masculinity.

nodes.name: Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer
nodes.summary: A comparison pairing an anxious, sweaty 'fan' with a calm Gigachad 'enjoyer' of the same thing.
nodes.check_note: Year from the March 2021 video spike; still-image versions may be slightly earlier.

nodes.name: Advice Dog
nodes.summary: A smiling puppy on a rainbow colour-wheel background, captioned with two lines of terrible advice, which started the Advice Animals genre.

nodes.name: Courage Wolf
nodes.summary: A snarling wolf on a colour wheel offering extreme, aggressive motivational advice.

nodes.name: Insanity Wolf
nodes.summary: A wild-eyed wolf on a colour wheel giving deranged, violent advice as an escalation of Courage Wolf.

nodes.name: Socially Awkward Penguin
nodes.summary: A penguin on a blue colour-wheel background captioned with an embarrassing social blunder.

nodes.name: Socially Awesome Penguin
nodes.summary: The same penguin on a red background, captioned with a socially smooth success.

nodes.name: Philosoraptor
nodes.summary: A drawing of a velociraptor pondering, captioned with a pseudo-profound question or pun.

nodes.name: Foul Bachelor Frog
nodes.summary: A frog in a bathrobe captioned with the lazy, unhygienic habits of a single man living alone.

nodes.name: Paranoid Parrot
nodes.summary: A startled parrot captioned with irrational everyday fears and suspicions.
nodes.check_note: Became popular in August 2010; first use may be earlier.

nodes.name: Success Kid
nodes.summary: A toddler on a beach clenching a fistful of sand, captioned with small personal victories.
nodes.check_note: Photo taken August 2007; the earlier 'I Hate Sandcastles' captions are dated 2008 by some sources and 2011 by others, and the 'Success Kid' reading spread around 2010-2011.

nodes.name: Scumbag Steve
nodes.summary: A photo of a young man in a sideways cap and fur coat captioned with selfish, mooching behaviour.

nodes.name: Good Guy Greg
nodes.summary: A smiling man with a joint captioned with unexpectedly considerate behaviour.

nodes.name: Actual Advice Mallard
nodes.summary: A mallard on a colour wheel offering genuinely useful life tips.

nodes.name: Malicious Advice Mallard
nodes.summary: The same mallard with a red head, offering advice designed to cause harm.

nodes.name: Bad Luck Brian
nodes.summary: An awkward school portrait of a teenager in a plaid vest captioned with absurd strokes of misfortune.

nodes.name: Ridiculously Photogenic Guy
nodes.summary: A marathon photo of a runner looking effortlessly handsome, captioned with things that go easily for good-looking people.

nodes.name: Confession Bear
nodes.summary: A sheepish-looking bear captioned with an embarrassing or unpopular personal admission.

nodes.name: Overly Attached Girlfriend
nodes.summary: A wide-eyed, intensely smiling young woman captioned with clingy, possessive relationship behaviour.

nodes.name: Distracted Boyfriend
nodes.summary: A stock photo of a man turning to look at another woman while his partner glares, with each person labelled to show a shift in loyalty.

nodes.name: Drake Hotline Bling
nodes.summary: Two stacked stills of Drake from the 'Hotline Bling' video, waving away the top caption and approving the bottom one.
nodes.check_note: Video released October 2015; the two-panel approve/reject format reportedly circulated on 4chan in late 2015 and spread widely in early 2016.
